record.title: Weave reports routing-conditioned GPU scheduling gains for MoE inference
record.summary: The September 18 preprint presents Weave, which uses post-routing information to allocate GPU streaming multiprocessors dynamically between communication and computation for each MoE layer. Its abstract reports a 2.89× geometric-mean speedup for MoE layers and 1.33× end-to-end speedup over five systems across six MoE models on 4×H100 SXM GPUs. These are author-reported results; the full baseline tables and implementation were not independently checked here, and no reproduction or evidence of transfer to other hardware was found.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that Weave dynamically assigns streaming multiprocessors to communication and computation after per-layer routing on 4×H100 SXM GPUs, reaching a 2.89× geometric-mean MoE-layer speedup and a 1.33× geometric-mean end-to-end speedup across six MoE models versus five named-as-state-of-the-art systems in the paper. These measurements are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced in this review.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported speedups come from one 4×H100 SXM configuration and have not been independently reproduced; transfer to other GPU fabrics, model sizes, traffic mixtures and serving objectives is unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If sustained in the reported multi-GPU MoE regime, routing-conditioned SM scheduling can materially improve inference efficiency and change kernel and serving-system design choices; the result is meaningful but remains bounded to one 4×H100 setup and author-reported measurements.
limitations: The cited 2.89× layer-level and 1.33× end-to-end geometric means are reported by the paper authors, not independently measured here.
The abstract identifies 4×H100 SXM and six MoE models but does not establish performance on other accelerator systems or workload distributions.
No public implementation or reproduction was inspected in this bounded review; claimed comparisons depend on the paper's baseline configurations.
brief.summary: The September 18 preprint presents Weave, which uses post-routing information to allocate GPU streaming multiprocessors dynamically between communication and computation for each MoE layer. Its abstract reports a 2.89× geometric-mean speedup for MoE layers and 1.33× end-to-end speedup over five systems across six MoE models on 4×H100 SXM GPUs. These are author-reported results; the full baseline tables and implementation were not independently checked here, and no reproduction or evidence of transfer to other hardware was found.

technical.claimed_result: On 4×H100 SXM across six MoE models, the paper reports 2.89× geometric-mean MoE-layer and 1.33× end-to-end speedups versus five baselines.
technical.compute_or_cost: Evaluation regime stated in the abstract: 4×H100 SXM GPUs; no compute cost or energy comparison was recovered.
technical.demonstrated_result: No result independently demonstrated in this activation. The cited measurements are claims reported in the primary preprint.
technical.implementation_status: Preprint describes a persistent MoE megakernel with routing-conditioned spatial and temporal SM schedulers; implementation/code availability was not verified.
technical.mechanism: Once expert routing is known, a lightweight cost model partitions SMs between communication and computation workers per layer and GPU, then coordinates them over time to reduce resource mismatch and idle bubbles.
technical.novelty: The paper's claimed contribution is fine-grained runtime scheduling conditioned on each layer's routing result, rather than a fixed communication/computation SM split.
technical.regime: MoE inference under expert parallelism, evaluated on 4×H100 SXM across six models.
technical.reproducibility: Primary abstract is accessible; implementation, complete baseline configuration and independent reproduction were not inspected.
technical.strongest_baseline: Five systems described by the authors as state-of-the-art; individual baseline identities and matched settings require full-paper table inspection.

brief.title: Weave reports routing-conditioned GPU scheduling gains for MoE inference
brief.why_it_matters: MoE inference spends time coordinating expert computation with dispatch and combine traffic. If Weave's author-reported result holds, adapting the communication/computation split after routing can reduce resource mismatch on each layer and improve end-to-end serving efficiency. The tested 4×H100 result does not establish transfer to other hardware, workloads or deployment objectives.
